title: The SDLC Was Designed for Humans
excerpt: AI agents are entering a software delivery system built around human speed, judgment, and accountability. The next SDLC needs machine-readable context, enforceable limits, reproducible environments, and new measures of safe work.
content_html:
I was doing research on what to build next in the AI world. I’ve done a few hobby projects that have gone nowhere. I was fishing for the next. I was looking for an interesting idea to implement. So, I decided to take a look at recent job descriptions to see what companies want and where they want to go.

To my surprise, companies in very different domains look like they are asking for similar capabilities. Initially, most of the conversation around AI driven development was about producing and understanding code. Now, the problems are gradually moving to agentic development. Job descriptions talk about skills and MCP, standardized environments, reusable patterns, service metadata and permissions. Then there is evaluation, traceability, audit and the cost of work done by LLMs. These are different industries, different names, but they appear to be converging on the same question. How do we get LLMs to do repeatable, trustworthy and usable work?

We’re well past the stage where LLMs were autocomplete. We’ve been putting them deeper and deeper into the SDLC. The bizarre thing is that producing software is starting to move beyond human speed, while the rest of the system still assumes a human is on the other side.

Where Human Approval

We Put AI Into the Old Machine

When we first interacted with LLMs, we put them into our existing human workflows. That was rather a practical approach. Now, with the advent of agentic workflows, they are expected to be side by side with humans. The trouble is that almost everything around software development was designed around humans. Our throughput, permissions, development environments, review systems and ownership models all fundamentally assume that the actor doing the work is a person.

Our existing system looked roughly as follows.

Classic SDLC

Agents are different, for one, there can be many, and they do not necessarily operate at human speed. One engineer can have several agents making changes at once. That changes the assumptions underneath our entire development pipeline.

A pull request assumes changes arrive slowly enough for another human to inspect them. CI capacity roughly follows the pace at which humans produce code. Service ownership assumes teams create software slowly enough to absorb it. Permissions assume the actor exercising them is a person who can be held accountable later. All of that starts to break when the worker is an agent, because our system was never designed for something that can produce this much shit this quickly.

Humans Have Been Filling the Gaps

Today, humans are filling the gaps. For instance, we have been writing our documentation in markdown files, even more, we have been even writing ticket description, designs in such a way. That helps give context for AI because it can then pattern search what happened.

We have also been building paved paths for years to repeat quality across repositories. The difference is that another consumer has arrived. Now, we need to do the same for LLMs but the trick is to get them to consume it. Companies are investing in reusable patterns, reference architectures, service metadata, machine-readable instructions, skills, templates, development environments and explicit context delivery. Hence, standardization and paved paths appear again and again.

A surprising amount of what we will call LLM-ready platform engineering is really the work of converting organizational knowledge into something a machine can consume. Things engineers used to learn from another engineer, infer from a repository, or discover by asking around now have to become explicit. We have wanted better documentation for years and there is never enough of it. Apparently agents are finally going to make us write the damn thing, pro bono.

The Developer Platform Gets a New Persona

If you think about modern platform engineering, we standardized a few good things. With the new persona coming in, we need to think a bunch of these capabilities in terms of agents. Standard questions like how do I deploy, how do I create a ticket, where are my logs, how do I get credentials, who owns this service and so forth need to be calibrated against both humans and agents.

Developer experience, AI platform, security and developer productivity are already bleeding into each other. I don’t think the names will matter for long. Call it whatever you want. We are going to end up with a platform that has to work for both humans and agents.

Once an agent needs to discover a service, figure out who owns it, get credentials, make a change and prove what it did, our concerns start collapsing into each other. Humans have been filling the gaps with judgment, memory, reputation and the ability to ask someone what the hell is going on. Agents need those things represented in the system.

Limits will be Part of Control Plane

Now, we are solving the problem of what LLMs are allowed to do and what they aren’t. If you wrote something as follows.

Use Java 24.  
Follow our repository pattern.  
Do not access production.  
Run integration tests.  
Ask before changing schemas.

We are using prose as permission and LLMs occasionally don't give a shit. If we are going to give an agent consequential work, that’s not gonna fly. These are also represented in every repo, so they will drift. I think these will converge into controlled permissions, policy, traceability, auditability, validation and reproducible environments alongside ordinary agent instructions. And again there seems to be startups around that. Missed the train!

One thing that I have never thought of is that instructions become executable constraints. That’s essentially what we wanted in platforms but we also valued engineering freedom to an extent. We are now treating this as non-negotiable given that agents can mess things up big time.

Rules like “Do not access production” or “Ask before changing schemas” can’t be soft prompts. The platform has to say no. Maybe that’s policy-as-code at the API layer, maybe something else, but the agent shouldn’t get to negotiate. The same goes for execution. If an agent gets a working tree, give it a reproducible, isolated environment too. A short-lived container, for example. Let it loop there instead of running its nonsense on shared infrastructure. And keep a record of what it did and why, because “it ran” isn’t much help when something goes wrong.

On the flip side, not every instruction needs enforcement. “Prefer this repository pattern” can remain guidance. Instructions can express taste. Anything that defines what an agent is allowed to do has to live in the platform constraints.

The Unit of Work Introduces New Metrics

Developer productivity was about enabling engineers to get their best work with the least amount of friction. We tracked a few good metrics such as lead time for changes, deployment frequency, change failure rate and so on. They became part of the DORA metrics. Yet metrics are indicators, not guarantees. With LLMs, I think something closer to time to safe merge starts becoming interesting because the developer is no longer necessarily the unit producing the work.

Suppose five agents are working for an engineer, assuming the token cost will go lower. Each agent gets a sandbox, a working tree. That means pressure on compiling, testing, and other resources because these agents can spend a lot of time doing the work, e.g. loop engineering. In the end, someone takes a look at the work and says this is ready.

The imbalance is interesting. Five agents can generate fifty candidate changes while the engineer is still one person who has to establish whether any of them are safe. We can increase production upstream without increasing safe throughput downstream. That means the metric cannot simply be how much code the agent produced or how many tasks it completed. The useful boundary is how much of the path to a safe merge the system can complete without creating more work for the human at the end.

What the Next SDLC Looks Like

This research made me ask the same question again and again. How does SDLC look like in the future? I think it has drastically changed for some companies already, not so much for others. Some companies are already defining an agentic SDLC while others are still putting agents into the existing one.

I think we are going to go to something like standardized environments, skills, permissions, evaluation and lifecycle controls rather than something the sources describe as one finished system. When you have a task like moving the payments service to the new authentication mechanism. It would look quite different. It’s more like as follows.

Agentic SDLC

In this world, agents become replaceable. It’s like switching from one electricity provider to another. The important point is that the surrounding engineering platform knows enough to let either of them work safely. In a few years, we came to a quite different place from where we started with coding assistants.

And once the platform knows enough to let an agent do the work, the interesting problems start moving outside the agent. Who can do what, what happens when work collides, who owns the result, and eventually, how the agents deal with each other.

What’s the Bottleneck?

Our development environments are assumed and designed for humans. If code takes thirty seconds and CI takes twenty minutes, CI becomes the problem. If five agents can work in parallel but their changes collide, integration becomes the problem. If agents can create services faster than teams can operate them, ownership becomes the problem. If agents can execute production actions, authorization becomes the problem. If agents can create hundreds of internal skills and workflows, lifecycle and reuse become the problem. More ifs to come. However, that’s not where this ends.

The bottleneck keeps moving because the constraint we removed was human production speed. We did not remove everything that surrounded it.

It comes back to a question I asked earlier: where does the automation have to stop? I thought the answer was humans, one way or another. Perhaps. The strange part is that the further we automate the SDLC, the more it starts to resemble the thing we were supposedly automating away. Good old engineering organization.

Parallel agents need to divide work without making the same bet. They need to distrust bad information, resolve conflicts, establish hierarchy and remember what happened. They also have to deal with actors whose goals do not quite line up. Humans have norms, reputation, incentives and recourse because intelligence is never enough to make coordination work.

It looks like agents are going to discover the same problem very quickly. So perhaps the final bottleneck is not only humans but also coordination of agents. We can replace more of the people doing the work, but then we have to rebuild, in software, many of the systems humans invented to make groups of people work together.

sentences.en: Things engineers used to learn from another engineer, infer from a repository, or discover by asking around now have to become explicit.
sentences.zh: 工程师过去从其他工程师那里学习、从存储库中推断或通过询问发现的东西现在必须变得明确。

sentences.en: We have wanted better documentation for years and there is never enough of it.
sentences.zh: 多年来我们一直想要更好的文档，但永远不够。

sentences.en: Apparently agents are finally going to make us write the damn thing, pro bono.
sentences.zh: 显然，特工们终于要让我们无偿地写出这该死的东西了。

blocks.html_en: The Developer Platform Gets a New Persona

sentences.en: The Developer Platform Gets a New Persona
sentences.zh: 开发者平台焕然一新

blocks.html_en: If you think about modern platform engineering, we standardized a few good things. With the new persona coming in, we need to think a bunch of these capabilities in terms of agents. Standard questions like how do I deploy, how do I create a ticket, where are my logs, how do I get credentials, who owns this service and so forth need to be calibrated against both humans and agents.

sentences.en: If you think about modern platform engineering, we standardized a few good things.
sentences.zh: 如果你考虑一下现代平台工程，我们标准化了一些好的东西。

sentences.en: With the new persona coming in, we need to think a bunch of these capabilities in terms of agents.
sentences.zh: 随着新角色的出现，我们需要考虑代理的一系列功能。

sentences.en: Standard questions like how do I deploy, how do I create a ticket, where are my logs, how do I get credentials, who owns this service and so forth need to be calibrated against both humans and agents.
sentences.zh: 标准问题（例如如何部署、如何创建票证、我的日志在哪里、如何获取凭据、谁拥有此服务等等）需要针对人和代理进行校准。

blocks.html_en: Developer experience, AI platform, security and developer productivity are already bleeding into each other. I don’t think the names will matter for long. Call it whatever you want. We are going to end up with a platform that has to work for both humans and agents.

sentences.en: Developer experience, AI platform, security and developer productivity are already bleeding into each other.
sentences.zh: 开发者体验、人工智能平台、安全性和开发者生产力已经相互渗透。

sentences.en: I don’t think the names will matter for long.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些名字不会长久重要。

sentences.en: Call it whatever you want.
sentences.zh: 随便你怎么称呼它。

sentences.en: We are going to end up with a platform that has to work for both humans and agents.
sentences.zh: 我们最终将得到一个必须同时适用于人类和代理的平台。

blocks.html_en: Once an agent needs to discover a service, figure out who owns it, get credentials, make a change and prove what it did, our concerns start collapsing into each other. Humans have been filling the gaps with judgment, memory, reputation and the ability to ask someone what the hell is going on. Agents need those things represented in the system.

sentences.en: Once an agent needs to discover a service, figure out who owns it, get credentials, make a change and prove what it did, our concerns start collapsing into each other.
sentences.zh: 一旦代理需要发现一项服务、弄清楚谁拥有它、获取凭证、进行更改并证明它做了什么，我们的担忧就开始相互冲突。

sentences.en: Humans have been filling the gaps with judgment, memory, reputation and the ability to ask someone what the hell is going on.
sentences.zh: 人类一直在用判断力、记忆力、声誉以及询问别人到底发生了什么的能力来填补这些空白。

sentences.en: Agents need those things represented in the system.
sentences.zh: 代理需要系统中代表的那些东西。

blocks.html_en: Limits will be Part of Control Plane

sentences.en: Limits will be Part of Control Plane
sentences.zh: 限制将成为控制平面的一部分

blocks.html_en: Now, we are solving the problem of what LLMs are allowed to do and what they aren’t. If you wrote something as follows.

sentences.en: Now, we are solving the problem of what LLMs are allowed to do and what they aren’t.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们正在解决法学硕士可以做什么和不可以做什么的问题。

sentences.en: If you wrote something as follows.
sentences.zh: 如果你写了如下内容。

blocks.html_en: We are using prose as permission and LLMs occasionally don't give a shit. If we are going to give an agent consequential work, that’s not gonna fly. These are also represented in every repo, so they will drift. I think these will converge into controlled permissions, policy, traceability, auditability, validation and reproducible environments alongside ordinary agent instructions. And again there seems to be startups around that. Missed the train!

sentences.en: We are using prose as permission and LLMs occasionally don't give a shit.
sentences.zh: 我们使用散文作为许可，而法学硕士有时根本不在乎。

sentences.en: If we are going to give an agent consequential work, that’s not gonna fly.
sentences.zh: 如果我们要给特工分配相应的工作，那是行不通的。

sentences.en: These are also represented in every repo, so they will drift.
sentences.zh: 这些也出现在每个存储库中，因此它们会发生变化。

sentences.en: I think these will converge into controlled permissions, policy, traceability, auditability, validation and reproducible environments alongside ordinary agent instructions.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些将与普通代理指令一起汇聚成受控权限、策略、可追溯性、可审计性、验证和可重现环境。

sentences.en: And again there seems to be startups around that.
sentences.zh: 似乎又出现了围绕这一点的初创公司。

sentences.en: Missed the train!
sentences.zh: 错过了火车！

blocks.html_en: One thing that I have never thought of is that instructions become executable constraints. That’s essentially what we wanted in platforms but we also valued engineering freedom to an extent. We are now treating this as non-negotiable given that agents can mess things up big time.

sentences.en: One thing that I have never thought of is that instructions become executable constraints.
sentences.zh: 我从未想到的一件事是指令成为可执行的约束。

sentences.en: That’s essentially what we wanted in platforms but we also valued engineering freedom to an extent.
sentences.zh: 这本质上就是我们想要的平台，但我们也在一定程度上重视工程自由度。

sentences.en: We are now treating this as non-negotiable given that agents can mess things up big time.
sentences.zh: 鉴于特工可能会把事情搞得一团糟，我们现在将此视为不可协商的事情。

blocks.html_en: Rules like “Do not access production” or “Ask before changing schemas” can’t be soft prompts. The platform has to say no. Maybe that’s policy-as-code at the API layer, maybe something else, but the agent shouldn’t get to negotiate. The same goes for execution. If an agent gets a working tree, give it a reproducible, isolated environment too. A short-lived container, for example. Let it loop there instead of running its nonsense on shared infrastructure. And keep a record of what it did and why, because “it ran” isn’t much help when something goes wrong.

sentences.en: Rules like “Do not access production” or “Ask before changing schemas” can’t be soft prompts.
sentences.zh: 像“不要访问生产”或“更改模式之前询问”这样的规则不能是软提示。

sentences.en: The platform has to say no.
sentences.zh: 平台不得不说不。

sentences.en: Maybe that’s policy-as-code at the API layer, maybe something else, but the agent shouldn’t get to negotiate.
sentences.zh: 也许这是 API 层的策略即代码，也许是其他东西，但代理不应该进行协商。

sentences.en: The same goes for execution.
sentences.zh: 执行也是如此。

sentences.en: If an agent gets a working tree, give it a reproducible, isolated environment too.
sentences.zh: 如果代理获得一棵工作树，也给它一个可重复的、隔离的环境。

sentences.en: A short-lived container, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，一个短暂的容器。

sentences.en: Let it loop there instead of running its nonsense on shared infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 让它在那里循环，而不是在共享基础设施上运行它的废话。

sentences.en: And keep a record of what it did and why, because “it ran” isn’t much help when something goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 并记录它做了什么以及为什么，因为当出现问题时“它运行了”并没有多大帮助。

blocks.html_en: On the flip side, not every instruction needs enforcement. “Prefer this repository pattern” can remain guidance. Instructions can express taste. Anything that defines what an agent is allowed to do has to live in the platform constraints.

sentences.en: On the flip side, not every instruction needs enforcement.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，并​​非每条指令都需要执行。

sentences.en: “Prefer this repository pattern” can remain guidance.
sentences.zh: “更喜欢这个存储库模式”可以仍然是指导。

sentences.en: Instructions can express taste.
sentences.zh: 说明可以表达品味。

sentences.en: Anything that defines what an agent is allowed to do has to live in the platform constraints.
sentences.zh: 任何定义允许代理做什么的事情都必须受到平台限制。

blocks.html_en: The Unit of Work Introduces New Metrics

sentences.en: The Unit of Work Introduces New Metrics
sentences.zh: 工作单元引入新指标

blocks.html_en: Developer productivity was about enabling engineers to get their best work with the least amount of friction. We tracked a few good metrics such as lead time for changes, deployment frequency, change failure rate and so on. They became part of the DORA metrics. Yet metrics are indicators, not guarantees. With LLMs, I think something closer to time to safe merge starts becoming interesting because the developer is no longer necessarily the unit producing the work.

sentences.en: Developer productivity was about enabling engineers to get their best work with the least amount of friction.
sentences.zh: 开发人员的生产力就是让工程师能够以最少的摩擦获得最好的工作。

sentences.en: We tracked a few good metrics such as lead time for changes, deployment frequency, change failure rate and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们跟踪了一些好的指标，例如变更的交付时间、部署频率、变更失败率等。

sentences.en: They became part of the DORA metrics.
sentences.zh: 它们成为 DORA 指标的一部分。

sentences.en: Yet metrics are indicators, not guarantees.
sentences.zh: 然而指标只是指标，而不是保证。

sentences.en: With LLMs, I think something closer to time to safe merge starts becoming interesting because the developer is no longer necessarily the unit producing the work.
sentences.zh: 对于法学硕士，我认为接近安全合并的事情开始变得有趣，因为开发人员不再一定是制作工作的单位。

blocks.html_en: Suppose five agents are working for an engineer, assuming the token cost will go lower. Each agent gets a sandbox, a working tree. That means pressure on compiling, testing, and other resources because these agents can spend a lot of time doing the work, e.g. loop engineering. In the end, someone takes a look at the work and says this is ready.

sentences.en: Suppose five agents are working for an engineer, assuming the token cost will go lower.
sentences.zh: 假设五个代理为一名工程师工作，假设代币成本会降低。

sentences.en: Each agent gets a sandbox, a working tree.
sentences.zh: 每个代理都有一个沙箱，一个工作树。

sentences.en: That means pressure on compiling, testing, and other resources because these agents can spend a lot of time doing the work, e.g. loop engineering.
sentences.zh: 这意味着编译、测试和其他资源上的压力，因为这些代理可能会花费大量时间来完成工作，例如循环工程。

sentences.en: In the end, someone takes a look at the work and says this is ready.
sentences.zh: 最后，有人看了一下作品，说已经准备好了。

blocks.html_en: The imbalance is interesting. Five agents can generate fifty candidate changes while the engineer is still one person who has to establish whether any of them are safe. We can increase production upstream without increasing safe throughput downstream. That means the metric cannot simply be how much code the agent produced or how many tasks it completed. The useful boundary is how much of the path to a safe merge the system can complete without creating more work for the human at the end.

sentences.en: The imbalance is interesting.
sentences.zh: 这种不平衡很有趣。

sentences.en: Five agents can generate fifty candidate changes while the engineer is still one person who has to establish whether any of them are safe.
sentences.zh: 五个代理可以生成五十个候选更改，而工程师仍然是一个必须确定其中任何一个是否安全的人。

sentences.en: We can increase production upstream without increasing safe throughput downstream.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在不增加下游安全吞吐量的情况下增加上游产量。

sentences.en: That means the metric cannot simply be how much code the agent produced or how many tasks it completed.
sentences.zh: 这意味着指标不能简单地是代理生成了多少代码或完成了多少任务。

sentences.en: The useful boundary is how much of the path to a safe merge the system can complete without creating more work for the human at the end.
sentences.zh: 有用的边界是系统可以完成多少安全合并路径，而最终不会为人类创造更多工作。

blocks.html_en: What the Next SDLC Looks Like

sentences.en: What the Next SDLC Looks Like
sentences.zh: 下一个 SDLC 是什么样子

blocks.html_en: This research made me ask the same question again and again. How does SDLC look like in the future? I think it has drastically changed for some companies already, not so much for others. Some companies are already defining an agentic SDLC while others are still putting agents into the existing one.

sentences.en: This research made me ask the same question again and again.
sentences.zh: 这项研究让我一次又一次地问同样的问题。

sentences.en: How does SDLC look like in the future?
sentences.zh: 未来的SDLC会是什么样子？

sentences.en: I think it has drastically changed for some companies already, not so much for others.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于一些公司来说已经发生了巨大的变化，而对于其他公司来说则没有那么大。

sentences.en: Some companies are already defining an agentic SDLC while others are still putting agents into the existing one.
sentences.zh: 一些公司已经定义了代理 SDLC，而另一些公司仍在将代理放入现有 SDLC 中。

blocks.html_en: I think we are going to go to something like standardized environments, skills, permissions, evaluation and lifecycle controls rather than something the sources describe as one finished system. When you have a task like moving the payments service to the new authentication mechanism. It would look quite different. It’s more like as follows.

sentences.en: I think we are going to go to something like standardized environments, skills, permissions, evaluation and lifecycle controls rather than something the sources describe as one finished system.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们将采用标准化环境、技能、权限、评估和生命周期控制之类的东西，而不是消息来源所描述的一个完整的系统。

sentences.en: When you have a task like moving the payments service to the new authentication mechanism.
sentences.zh: 当您有一项任务，例如将支付服务转移到新的身份验证机制时。

sentences.en: It would look quite different.
sentences.zh: 看起来会很不一样。

sentences.en: It’s more like as follows.
sentences.zh: 更像是如下所示。

blocks.html_en: Agentic SDLC

sentences.en: Agentic SDLC
sentences.zh: 代理SDLC

blocks.html_en: In this world, agents become replaceable. It’s like switching from one electricity provider to another. The important point is that the surrounding engineering platform knows enough to let either of them work safely. In a few years, we came to a quite different place from where we started with coding assistants.

sentences.en: In this world, agents become replaceable.
sentences.zh: 在这个世界上，代理人是可以替代的。

sentences.en: It’s like switching from one electricity provider to another.
sentences.zh: 这就像从一家电力供应商切换到另一家电力供应商一样。

sentences.en: The important point is that the surrounding engineering platform knows enough to let either of them work safely.
sentences.zh: 重要的一点是，周围的工程平台知道足够的信息，可以让它们中的任何一个安全地工作。

sentences.en: In a few years, we came to a quite different place from where we started with coding assistants.
sentences.zh: 几年后，我们来到了一个与最初使用编码助手的地方截然不同的地方。

blocks.html_en: And once the platform knows enough to let an agent do the work, the interesting problems start moving outside the agent. Who can do what, what happens when work collides, who owns the result, and eventually, how the agents deal with each other.

sentences.en: And once the platform knows enough to let an agent do the work, the interesting problems start moving outside the agent.
sentences.zh: 一旦平台足够了解让代理完成工作，有趣的问题就开始转移到代理之外。

sentences.en: Who can do what, what happens when work collides, who owns the result, and eventually, how the agents deal with each other.
sentences.zh: 谁能做什么，工作发生冲突时会发生什么，谁拥有结果，以及最终，代理人如何处理彼此。

blocks.html_en: What’s the Bottleneck?

sentences.en: What’s the Bottleneck?
sentences.zh: 瓶颈是什么？

blocks.html_en: Our development environments are assumed and designed for humans. If code takes thirty seconds and CI takes twenty minutes, CI becomes the problem. If five agents can work in parallel but their changes collide, integration becomes the problem. If agents can create services faster than teams can operate them, ownership becomes the problem. If agents can execute production actions, authorization becomes the problem. If agents can create hundreds of internal skills and workflows, lifecycle and reuse become the problem. More ifs to come. However, that’s not where this ends.

sentences.en: Our development environments are assumed and designed for humans.
sentences.zh: 我们的开发环境是为人类假设和设计的。

sentences.en: If code takes thirty seconds and CI takes twenty minutes, CI becomes the problem.
sentences.zh: 如果代码需要三十秒而 CI 需要二十分钟，那么 CI 就会成为问题。

sentences.en: If five agents can work in parallel but their changes collide, integration becomes the problem.
sentences.zh: 如果五个代理可以并行工作，但它们的更改发生冲突，那么集成就会成为问题。

sentences.en: If agents can create services faster than teams can operate them, ownership becomes the problem.
sentences.zh: 如果代理创建服务的速度比团队运营服务的速度快，那么所有权就会成为问题。

sentences.en: If agents can execute production actions, authorization becomes the problem.
sentences.zh: 如果代理可以执行生产操作，授权就成为问题。

sentences.en: If agents can create hundreds of internal skills and workflows, lifecycle and reuse become the problem.
sentences.zh: 如果代理可以创建数百个内部技能和工作流程，那么生命周期和重用就会成为问题。

sentences.en: More ifs to come.
sentences.zh: 更多假设即将到来。

sentences.en: However, that’s not where this ends.
sentences.zh: 然而，这并不是结束。

blocks.html_en: The bottleneck keeps moving because the constraint we removed was human production speed. We did not remove everything that surrounded it.

sentences.en: The bottleneck keeps moving because the constraint we removed was human production speed.
sentences.zh: 瓶颈不断移动，因为我们消除了人类生产速度的限制。

sentences.en: We did not remove everything that surrounded it.
sentences.zh: 我们没有移除它周围的所有东西。

blocks.html_en: It comes back to a question I asked earlier: where does the automation have to stop? I thought the answer was humans, one way or another. Perhaps. The strange part is that the further we automate the SDLC, the more it starts to resemble the thing we were supposedly automating away. Good old engineering organization.

sentences.en: It comes back to a question I asked earlier: where does the automation have to stop?
sentences.zh: 这又回到了我之前提出的一个问题：自动化必须在哪里停止？

sentences.en: I thought the answer was humans, one way or another.
sentences.zh: 我认为答案是人类，无论如何。

sentences.en: Perhaps.
sentences.zh: 也许。

sentences.en: The strange part is that the further we automate the SDLC, the more it starts to resemble the thing we were supposedly automating away.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，我们对 SDLC 的自动化程度越高，它就越开始像我们原本应该自动化的东西。

sentences.en: Good old engineering organization.
sentences.zh: 良好的旧工程组织。

blocks.html_en: Parallel agents need to divide work without making the same bet. They need to distrust bad information, resolve conflicts, establish hierarchy and remember what happened. They also have to deal with actors whose goals do not quite line up. Humans have norms, reputation, incentives and recourse because intelligence is never enough to make coordination work.

sentences.en: Parallel agents need to divide work without making the same bet.
sentences.zh: 并行代理需要分工而不进行相同的赌注。

sentences.en: They need to distrust bad information, resolve conflicts, establish hierarchy and remember what happened.
sentences.zh: 他们需要不信任不良信息、解决冲突、建立等级制度并记住发生的事情。

sentences.en: They also have to deal with actors whose goals do not quite line up.
sentences.zh: 他们还必须应对目标不一致的演员。

sentences.en: Humans have norms, reputation, incentives and recourse because intelligence is never enough to make coordination work.
sentences.zh: 人类有规范、声誉、激励和追索权，因为智力永远不足以使协调发挥作用。

blocks.html_en: It looks like agents are going to discover the same problem very quickly. So perhaps the final bottleneck is not only humans but also coordination of agents. We can replace more of the people doing the work, but then we have to rebuild, in software, many of the systems humans invented to make groups of people work together.

sentences.en: It looks like agents are going to discover the same problem very quickly.
sentences.zh: 看起来代理商很快就会发现同样的问题。

sentences.en: So perhaps the final bottleneck is not only humans but also coordination of agents.
sentences.zh: 因此，也许最终的瓶颈不仅是人类，还包括智能体的协调。

sentences.en: We can replace more of the people doing the work, but then we have to rebuild, in software, many of the systems humans invented to make groups of people work together.
sentences.zh: 我们可以取代更多的工作人员，但随后我们必须在软件中重建人类发明的许多系统，以使人们能够一起工作。

content_html_zh:
我正在研究人工智能世界的下一步发展。 我做过一些业余爱好项目，但都没有进展。 我正在钓鱼下一个。 我一直在寻找一个有趣的想法来实施。 因此，我决定看一下最近的职位描述，看看公司想要什么以及他们想去哪里。

令我惊讶的是，不同领域的公司看起来都要求类似的功能。 最初，围绕人工智能驱动开发的大部分讨论都是关于生成和理解代码。 现在，问题正逐渐转向代理开发。 职位描述涉及技能和 MCP、标准化环境、可重用模式、服务元数据和权限。 然后是评估、可追溯性、审计和法学硕士所做的工作成本。 这些是不同的行业，不同的名称，但它们似乎都集中在同一个问题上。 我们如何让法学硕士做可重复、值得信赖和可用的工作？

我们已经远远超过了法学硕士自动完成的阶段。 我们一直在将它们越来越深入地融入到 SDLC 中。 奇怪的是，软件的生产速度开始超越人类的速度，而系统的其余部分仍然假设人类在另一边。

人类认可的地方

我们将人工智能放入旧机器中

当我们第一次与法学硕士互动时，我们将他们纳入我们现有的人工工作流程中。 这是一个相当实用的方法。 现在，随着代理工作流程的出现，它们有望与人类并肩作战。 问题在于，几乎所有与软件开发相关的事情都是围绕人类设计的。 我们的吞吐量、权限、开发环境、审查系统和所有权模型都从根本上假设执行工作的参与者是一个人。

我们现有的系统大致如下。

经典SDLC

代理是不同的，一方面，可以有很多，而且他们不一定以人类的速度运作。 一名工程师可以让多名代理同时进行更改。 这改变了我们整个开发流程的假设。

拉取请求假设更改到达的速度足够慢，足以让另一个人检查它们。 CI 容量大致跟随着人类编写代码的速度。 服务所有权假设团队创建软件的速度足够慢以吸收它。 权限假设行使权限的人是一个可以在以后追究责任的人。 当工作人员成为代理时，所有这一切都开始被打破，因为我们的系统从来就不是为能够如此快速地产生这么多垃圾的东西而设计的。

人类一直在填补空白

今天，人类正在填补这一空白。 例如，我们一直在用markdown文件来编写我们的文档，甚至我们甚至用这样的方式来编写票据描述、设计。 这有助于为人工智能提供背景信息，因为它可以对发生的事情进行模式搜索。

多年来，我们还一直在构建铺平的道路，以在存储库中重复质量。 不同的是，另一个消费者已经到来。 现在，我们需要对法学硕士做同样的事情，但诀窍是让他们接受它。 公司正在投资可重用模式、参考架构、服务元数据、机器可读指令、技能、模板、开发环境和显式上下文交付。 因此，标准化和铺好的道路一次又一次地出现。

令人惊讶的是，我们所说的LLM就绪平台工程实际上是将组织知识转化为机器可以使用的东西的工作。 工程师过去从其他工程师那里学习、从存储库中推断或通过询问发现的东西现在必须变得明确。 多年来我们一直想要更好的文档，但永远不够。 显然，特工们终于要让我们无偿地写出这该死的东西了。

开发者平台焕然一新

如果你考虑一下现代平台工程，我们标准化了一些好的东西。 随着新角色的出现，我们需要考虑代理的一系列功能。 标准问题（例如如何部署、如何创建票证、我的日志在哪里、如何获取凭据、谁拥有此服务等等）需要针对人和代理进行校准。

开发者体验、人工智能平台、安全性和开发者生产力已经相互渗透。 我认为这些名字不会长久重要。 随便你怎么称呼它。 我们最终将得到一个必须同时适用于人类和代理的平台。

一旦代理需要发现一项服务、弄清楚谁拥有它、获取凭证、进行更改并证明它做了什么，我们的担忧就开始相互冲突。 人类一直在用判断力、记忆力、声誉以及询问别人到底发生了什么的能力来填补这些空白。 代理需要系统中代表的那些东西。

限制将成为控制平面的一部分

现在，我们正在解决法学硕士可以做什么和不可以做什么的问题。 如果你写了如下内容。

Use Java 24.  
Follow our repository pattern.  
Do not access production.  
Run integration tests.  
Ask before changing schemas.

我们使用散文作为许可，而法学硕士有时根本不在乎。 如果我们要给特工分配相应的工作，那是行不通的。 这些也出现在每个存储库中，因此它们会发生变化。 我认为这些将与普通代理指令一起汇聚成受控权限、策略、可追溯性、可审计性、验证和可重现环境。 似乎又出现了围绕这一点的初创公司。 错过了火车！

我从未想到的一件事是指令成为可执行的约束。 这本质上就是我们想要的平台，但我们也在一定程度上重视工程自由度。 鉴于特工可能会把事情搞得一团糟，我们现在将此视为不可协商的事情。

像“不要访问生产”或“更改模式之前询问”这样的规则不能是软提示。 平台不得不说不。 也许这是 API 层的策略即代码，也许是其他东西，但代理不应该进行协商。 执行也是如此。 如果代理获得一棵工作树，也给它一个可重复的、隔离的环境。 例如，一个短暂的容器。 让它在那里循环，而不是在共享基础设施上运行它的废话。 并记录它做了什么以及为什么，因为当出现问题时“它运行了”并没有多大帮助。

另一方面，并​​非每条指令都需要执行。 “更喜欢这个存储库模式”可以仍然是指导。 说明可以表达品味。 任何定义允许代理做什么的事情都必须受到平台限制。

工作单元引入新指标

开发人员的生产力就是让工程师能够以最少的摩擦获得最好的工作。 我们跟踪了一些好的指标，例如变更的交付时间、部署频率、变更失败率等。 它们成为 DORA 指标的一部分。 然而指标只是指标，而不是保证。 对于法学硕士，我认为接近安全合并的事情开始变得有趣，因为开发人员不再一定是制作工作的单位。

假设五个代理为一名工程师工作，假设代币成本会降低。 每个代理都有一个沙箱，一个工作树。 这意味着编译、测试和其他资源上的压力，因为这些代理可能会花费大量时间来完成工作，例如循环工程。 最后，有人看了一下作品，说已经准备好了。

这种不平衡很有趣。 五个代理可以生成五十个候选更改，而工程师仍然是一个必须确定其中任何一个是否安全的人。 我们可以在不增加下游安全吞吐量的情况下增加上游产量。 这意味着指标不能简单地是代理生成了多少代码或完成了多少任务。 有用的边界是系统可以完成多少安全合并路径，而最终不会为人类创造更多工作。

下一个 SDLC 是什么样子

这项研究让我一次又一次地问同样的问题。 未来的SDLC会是什么样子？ 我认为对于一些公司来说已经发生了巨大的变化，而对于其他公司来说则没有那么大。 一些公司已经定义了代理 SDLC，而另一些公司仍在将代理放入现有 SDLC 中。

我认为我们将采用标准化环境、技能、权限、评估和生命周期控制之类的东西，而不是消息来源所描述的一个完整的系统。 当您有一项任务，例如将支付服务转移到新的身份验证机制时。 看起来会很不一样。 更像是如下所示。

代理SDLC

在这个世界上，代理人是可以替代的。 这就像从一家电力供应商切换到另一家电力供应商一样。 重要的一点是，周围的工程平台知道足够的信息，可以让它们中的任何一个安全地工作。 几年后，我们来到了一个与最初使用编码助手的地方截然不同的地方。

一旦平台足够了解让代理完成工作，有趣的问题就开始转移到代理之外。 谁能做什么，工作发生冲突时会发生什么，谁拥有结果，以及最终，代理人如何处理彼此。

瓶颈是什么？

我们的开发环境是为人类假设和设计的。 如果代码需要三十秒而 CI 需要二十分钟，那么 CI 就会成为问题。 如果五个代理可以并行工作，但它们的更改发生冲突，那么集成就会成为问题。 如果代理创建服务的速度比团队运营服务的速度快，那么所有权就会成为问题。 如果代理可以执行生产操作，授权就成为问题。 如果代理可以创建数百个内部技能和工作流程，那么生命周期和重用就会成为问题。 更多假设即将到来。 然而，这并不是结束。

瓶颈不断移动，因为我们消除了人类生产速度的限制。 我们没有移除它周围的所有东西。

这又回到了我之前提出的一个问题：自动化必须在哪里停止？ 我认为答案是人类，无论如何。 也许。 奇怪的是，我们对 SDLC 的自动化程度越高，它就越开始像我们原本应该自动化的东西。 良好的旧工程组织。

并行代理需要分工而不进行相同的赌注。 他们需要不信任不良信息、解决冲突、建立等级制度并记住发生的事情。 他们还必须应对目标不一致的演员。 人类有规范、声誉、激励和追索权，因为智力永远不足以使协调发挥作用。

看起来代理商很快就会发现同样的问题。 因此，也许最终的瓶颈不仅是人类，还包括智能体的协调。 我们可以取代更多的工作人员，但随后我们必须在软件中重建人类发明的许多系统，以使人们能够一起工作。
